name: Context-Based Adaptive Ray Sampling with Quadtree Subdivision
definition: A training-stage sampling strategy that uses a quadtree to partition the image space, sampling more rays in nontrivial areas (high color change/high rendering error) and fewer in trivial areas to reduce training burden while capturing details.
summary: Context-Based Adaptive Ray Sampling with Quadtree Subdivision is a training-stage strategy that partitions image space into a quadtree to allocate ray density based on local rendering error, using prior and posterior probability distributions to guide sampling and prune redundant blocks.
